Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:17: The reward of a person who crowns the Holy One, blessed be He, over every single limb is reckoned as though he had crowned Him over the whole world, since a person is called a small world, and permission has not been given to reveal the reward for the reasons of the commandments, so that a person not serve the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to receive a reward. But come and see — that judgment depends upon the speech of the mouth and likewise upon the eyes, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said, "a judge has only what his eyes see." Sacrifices, which are a pleasing fragrance to the Lord, and the fragrant woods of Havdalah, depend upon the nose. The recitation of the Shema and the hearing of the shofar, and all commandments concerning which it is said, "if he made it heard to his own ear, he has fulfilled his duty," depend upon the ears. Tefillin depend upon the head, and all the commandments are bound to one another. And in the Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Naso: when a human being performs even a single commandment — no more — in fear and love of the Holy One, blessed be He, on account of that commandment the ten sefirot rest upon him, and whoever fulfills a commandment as required, it is as though he fulfilled all 248 positive commandments, since there is no commandment that is not included in all 248, as above. The reward of a person who crowns the Holy One, blessed be He, over every limb is reckoned as though he had crowned Him over the whole world, since a person is called a small world. And permission has not been given to reveal the reward of the reasons of the commandments, so that a person not serve the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to receive reward. But come and see that soul which is in the image of its Master, that fulfills all these His commandments — when it ascends on high, all the hosts of angels that depend on these commandments, and all the corrections and encampments of the King's body, ascend with it, and when it descends they all descend with it, and it is the ladder of which it is said (Genesis 28:12), "and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending upon it," and a voice descends through all the heights of the heavens: "Give honor to the image of the King."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:18: The commandment of circumcision, just as it removes those kelipot from that limb and prepares a place for the Shechinah to dwell, so too, when the soul ascends on high, it ascends in the Name Havayah, and all kelipot and destroying angels are removed from it, so that they cannot approach it.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:19: And just as one occupies oneself with Torah and commandments, called "light" and "candle," so likewise when a person goes to that world (Exodus 13:21), "and the Lord went before them" — his soul, his spirit, and his life-breath — in a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire to guide them along the way, to give them light.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:20: And just as one keeps the Sabbath, and rests, and delights in it for the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, so is he given, above, a place of rest, and there he rests from all he labored for in this world:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:21: Whoever unifies the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah — the Holy One, blessed be He, unites him with his soulmate in that world. Whoever draws the Shechinah near to himself — so it is with the fulfillment of all these his commandments. When it ascends on high, all the hosts of angels that depend on those commandments, and all the corrections and dwellings drawn from the King's body, ascend with it, and when it descends, all descend with it, and it is the ladder of which it is said, "and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending upon it." And a voice passes through all the heights of the heavens: "Give honor to the image of the King." The commandment of circumcision — just as it removes those kelipot from that limb and prepared a place for the dwelling of the Shechinah, so too the soul, when it ascends on high, ascends in the Name Havayah, and removes from itself all the kelipot and destroying angels so that they do not come near it. And just as one occupies oneself with Torah and commandments, called "light" and "candle," so too when he goes to that world, then the Lord goes before his soul, his spirit, and his life-breath in a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire, to guide them along the way, to give them light. And just as one keeps the Sabbath and rests and delights in it for the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, so too the soul shall receive above a place of rest and shall rest there from all that it labored for in this world. Whoever unifies the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah — the Holy One, blessed be He, unites him with his soulmate in the World to Come. Whoever draws the Shechinah near to himself, so likewise is his soulmate drawn near to him; and whoever makes himself a sanctuary — so likewise is a chamber of the Holy of Holies made for him, in which to dwell.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:22: Whoever builds a sukkah — the Holy One, blessed be He, will shelter and protect him from all destroying angels and accusers when he departs from this world.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:23: Whoever recites the seven blessings of the Shema and sanctifies Him with "Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh" and unifies Him in the Shema — so too He shall bless him and sanctify him with the ten wedding canopies in the Garden of Eden and unify him with his own bride.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:24: Whoever prepares a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He, by wrapping himself in the tallit of the commandment, and crowns himself with tefillin, and calls out "Shema Yisrael" so that the Holy One, blessed be He, may sit upon His throne — so too He shall prepare for him, in that world, a throne and a crown of royal kingship, and shall make him king over all the angels and hosts there. And just as he gives satisfaction to the Holy One, blessed be He, through songs, hymns, praises, and thanksgivings, and causes Him to dwell in this world, so too when he ascends there, all the living creatures of the Chariot, and the hosts of angels — living creatures, seraphim, and ofanim — shall spread their wings to receive him with joy and with song:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:25: In the end, no mouth is able to declare his reward in that world, throughout all generations. Happy is he who causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to dwell in every one of his limbs, that none of his limbs remain vacant, without His presence resting upon it, so that he must sanctify Him and make of himself a house of the Holy of Holies for Him to dwell within. He who builds a sukkah — the Holy One, blessed be He, shall shelter and protect him from every destroying angel and accuser when he leaves this world. He who recites the seven blessings of the Shema and sanctifies the Holy One, blessed be He, with "Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh," and unifies Him in the recitation of the Shema — so too shall the Holy One, blessed be He, bless him and sanctify him with the ten wedding canopies of betrothal in the Garden of Eden, and unify him with his own bride. He who prepares a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapping himself in the tallit of the commandment, and crowns himself with tefillin, and calls out "Shema Yisrael" so that the Holy One, blessed be He, may dwell upon His throne — so too shall the Holy One, blessed be He, prepare for him, in the World to Come, a throne and a crown of royal kingship, and make him king over all the angels and hosts there. And just as one gives satisfaction to the Holy One, blessed be He, through songs, hymns, and thanksgivings, and causes Him to dwell in this world, so too, when he ascends there, all the living creatures of the Chariots and the hosts of angels — living creatures, seraphim, and ofanim — shall spread their wings to receive him with joy and with melody. In the end, no mouth can say his reward in that world for all generations. Happy is he who causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to dwell in all his limbs, for if even one limb of his lacks His presence and He does not rest upon it, on account of that limb he must return in reincarnation to this world, until he is completed in all his limbs, in the image of the divine likeness — for if he lacks even one, he is not in that image.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:26: In the end, everything that a person labors for should be for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, when he performs His commandments, and so, measure for measure, the Holy One, blessed be He, shall labor for his sake and for the sake of his soulmate in that world:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:27: [Translation — Every prophet and every human being, each ascends to his own limb from which his soul was hewn. Some of them are in the head of the King, some in the strands of hair, in the eyes, in the ears, in the face, in the nose, in the mouth, in the neck, in the hands, in the stature of the person which is the body, in the thighs, in the loins, in the legs, in the sign of the covenant, in the brain, in the heart. And every one of these limbs has its own known sefirah among the ten sefirot, and all these limbs depend upon the image of the King's body, and there is one whose soul comes from the King's garments. And all 613 commandments of the Torah are dependent upon these limbs of the King's body — there are commandments dependent on the head of the King, and there are commandments dependent on the eyes, and so on. And every commandment that rests upon each and every limb has its own known name, and within it is the Name Havayah, which is the soul of that limb, and all the limbs are called appellations for the Name Havayah, which is within every limb, and every name and appellation of every limb has power only over that limb of its own. But the Holy One, blessed be He, the Name Havayah — His power is in every place, like a soul that rules over every limb; and this is [the meaning of] "the whole earth is full of His glory." And every commandment that a person performs not in order to receive reward depends upon the image of the King in the World of Atzilut, but commandments performed in order to receive reward depend upon the image of that which is called 'the youth' above. And on every limb of the King's image depend several angels called 'the eyes of the Lord,' 'the ears of the Lord,' 'the hands of the Lord,' and so on, and all of them depend from the King's body like strands of hair that hang down from the head. And every strand of hair is one angel, and the 613 limbs of a person are all arranged according to the order of Creation, and for this reason a person is called a small world. And through every commandment a person performs he causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to be crowned as King over that limb of the person's soul, corresponding to that commandment. And every limb of the soul is called a candle, as it is written, "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" — through it he performs that commandment, and so the commandment too is called a candle, as it is written, "for the commandment is a candle."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:28: A person must remove from all his limbs all bad thoughts, which are the kelipot that dwell within a person, and must prepare a clean, pure place there for the Holy One, blessed be He, to dwell — for any limb that is blemished by a sin a person commits, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not dwell in that limb, as it is written, "for any man in whom there is a blemish shall not draw near." And whoever blemishes even one commandment, it is as though he committed treason against the image of the King. He must burn away those kelipot that dwell there, among the commandments that dwell upon each and every limb, and remove them, for they are called leaven and chametz, through these candles, of which it is said, "for the commandment is a candle," and it is written, "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man, searching all the chambers of the innards." And when the Holy One, blessed be He — who is the Name Havayah, blessed be He, and His appellations called His limbs — dwells there, the hosts of angels that depend on that limb guard that limb against all the bad things and kelipot that had dwelt there. There are commandments that depend, and so on — every commandment of fear and love depends upon the brain and the heart; every commandment of walking depends upon the legs, such as walking to the synagogue, to a circumcision, to accompany the dead, or to any walking for the sake of a commandment. And those who stand in the standing position of the Amidah prayer, upon their two legs:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:1-3: On the punishment for bad character traits, and the reward for acquiring good ones:

Pride is a root of many transgressions, whether between man and the Omnipresent or between man and his fellow, for it causes him to harm his fellow, to hate him, and to speak evil speech of him, and many things like these; and as between him and the Omnipresent, it is likewise written (Deuteronomy 8:14), "and your heart grows haughty and you forget the Lord your God," and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 5a), "whoever possesses haughtiness of spirit is called an abomination," as it is said (Proverbs 16:5), "every haughty heart is an abomination to the Lord." And they said, "he is under a ban, whoever possesses it," and he deserves to be hewn down like an Asherah, and even his dust shall not be stirred, and the Shechinah wails over him, and he is equal to an idolater and a heretic, and it is as though he had violated all forbidden sexual relations, and as though he had built a high place [for idol worship]; and even if he were to acquire heaven and earth for the Holy One, blessed be He, like our father Abraham, he would not be acquitted from the judgment of Gehinnom, and his end is to be diminished and gathered from the world before his time,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:4: and even Jeroboam — before whom all the sages of his generation were as the grass of the field (Sanhedrin 102a), and there was no flaw in his Torah learning, and he expounded the Torah in one hundred and fifty ways — was punished on account of pride, and driven from this world and the World to Come. For if not one limb remains vacant, without the Holy One, blessed be He, resting upon it, then on account of that limb one must return in reincarnation to this world, until he is completed in all his limbs, in the image of God's likeness — for if he lacks even one, he is not in His image. In the end, whatever a person labors for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, so, measure for measure, does the Holy One, blessed be He, labor for his sake and for the sake of his soulmate in that world. He is punished and banished from this world and the World to Come only because of haughtiness of spirit, as though he were pushing away the feet of the Shechinah, causing her to depart from the world and to say, "I and he cannot dwell together in the world."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:5: He rebels against the Kingdom of Heaven, and wraps himself in the garment of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is said (Psalms 93:1), "the Lord reigns, He is clothed in majesty (ge'ut)" — and in what should a person be proud, when his existence began from a putrid drop, his formation was in the blood of menstruation, and his life is filth and stench, and after his death he is maggot and worm, and the end of his body is a clod of earth, and his soul descends to Gehinnom:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:6: But humility and lowliness — there is no greater trait than these, for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the master of all the prophets, was praised, in Torah, in commandments, and in fear of sin, only for his humility, as it is said (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was exceedingly humble." Go and learn from the Holy One, blessed be He, who left the highest heavens and came down to dwell among the lowly, as it is said (Isaiah 57:15), "I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with him who is of a contrite and lowly spirit," and it is written (Psalms 34:19), "the Lord is near to the brokenhearted," and it is written (ibid. 15:1), "Who shall dwell in Your tent..." — "in whose eyes a vile person is despised."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:7: And although it is written of the fear [of Heaven] (Job 28:28), "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom," and it is written (Isaiah 33:6), "the fear of the Lord is His treasure," our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:3), it is the very heel of humility, as it is written (Proverbs 22:4), "the heel of humility is the fear of the Lord,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:8: and whoever holds his own mind lowly, it is as though he had offered all the sacrifices, as it is said (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit," and moreover, his prayer is not despised, for a person's prayer is heard only if he makes himself like flesh (Sotah 5a), as it is said (Isaiah 66:23), "and it shall be, from new moon to new moon... all flesh shall come to worship," and it is written (ibid. 66:2), "but to this one will I look, to the poor and the contrite of spirit."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:9: And whoever is humble causes the Shechinah to rest upon man on earth, as it is said (Exodus 20:18), "and Moses drew near to the thick darkness" — what caused this for him? His humility, as it is said (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was exceedingly humble":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:10: And it was taught, Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says (end of Sotah): watchfulness leads to alacrity, and alacrity leads to cleanliness, and cleanliness leads to purity, and purity leads to abstinence, and abstinence leads to holiness, and holiness leads to humility, and so on, and humility is greater than all of them, for it brings one to the Holy Spirit, as it is said (Isaiah 61:1), "the spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:11: And a message was sent from there (Sanhedrin 88a): Who has a share in the World to Come? One who is humble and lowly, who bends low when entering and bends low when leaving, and studies Torah constantly, and does not take credit for himself. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to be a crown upon the head of every tzaddik, and so on; one might think for everyone — Scripture teaches (Isaiah 28:5), "to the remnant of His people" — to whoever regards himself as a remnant:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:12: And in Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Shelach (161a), thus began the head of the academy: Happy is he who makes himself small in this world, how great he shall be in that world; whoever is small is great, and whoever is great is small. Further there, Parashat Terumah (166): why is Ezekiel called "son of Buzi"? Because he would make himself lowly before whoever was greater than him, and for this he merited to be called "son of man" (ben adam), which no other person was ever called; and he was called "lofty," as it is written (Job 32:2), "Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram," and so on,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:13: and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 7a): why was the Torah likened to water? Just as water flows only to a low place, so too the Torah rests only on one whose spirit is lowly. Happy is he who is not quick to anger, and whose spirit is exceedingly lowly and humble, as it is said (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit." Happy is he who is patient toward everyone, bearing everything favorably for the sake of his Maker's will, and makes himself as a remnant, as it is said (Micah 7:18), "who bears iniquity and passes over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance" — for whoever regards himself as a remnant. Happy is the person who makes himself like dust, which everyone tramples, and who is like the lowest threshold, upon which everyone treads, and like the lowest peg, from which everyone hangs, and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:14: <small>[Translation — In Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Shelach, thus began the head of the academy to expound: happy is he who makes himself small in this world, how great is he in the World to Come. Whoever is small is great, and whoever is great is small. Further there, in Parashat Terumah: why was he called Ezekiel son of Buzi? Because he would make himself lowly before whoever was greater than himself. And for this he merited to be called "son of man," which no other person was ever called; and he was called "lofty," as it is written, "Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram."]</small>:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:15: Anger is a branch of pride, and is weighed as equal to it. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Nedarim 22a), whoever becomes angry — every kind of punishment of Gehinnom rules over him; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 105b), whoever tears his garments, scatters his money, or breaks vessels in his rage, should be in your eyes like an idolater, as it is said (Psalms 81:10), "there shall be no strange god within you,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:16: and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Nedarim 22b), whoever becomes angry — the Shechinah is not important compared to him, and he forgets his learning and increases his foolishness, and it is known that his sins outweigh his merits, as it is said (Proverbs 29:22), "and a man of wrath abounds in transgression"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 66b), whoever becomes angry, if he is a sage, his wisdom departs from him — how do we know this? From Moses and from Elisha, and so on; and Elijah, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 29b) to Rav Yehuda, "Do not become heated and you will not sin,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:17: and in the Zohar, Parashat Tetzaveh (182a, 263b): if a person becomes angry, his supernal holy soul is uprooted from him, so that the sitra achra (the Other Side) may rest in its place, and this is a person who rebels against his Master, and it is forbidden to draw near to him — and this is [the meaning of] "he tears his own soul in his anger," for he tears his own soul and settles a strange god in its place. For what is he then reckoned? He is called idolatry itself, and whoever converses with him is as though he had joined himself to actual idolatry, for actual idolatry dwells within him; and it is forbidden to gaze upon his face, and of him it is written (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to idols," and concerning this it is written (Exodus 34:17), "you shall not make for yourself molten gods."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:18: And all forms of impurity have a purification except this one, since it defiles the body from within and from without, and defiles the entire soul. And even if this person comes and completely uproots that strange [spirit] from within himself forever, and afterward strives to sanctify himself and to draw down that holy soul upon himself once more — even then, would that he be sanctified, for since it once fled from him, how much must a person do until it returns to its place:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:19: [Translation — In the Zohar, Parashat Tetzaveh: if a person becomes angry, he uproots from himself a supernal holy soul, so that the sitra achra dwells in its place, and this is a person who rebels against his Master and it is forbidden to be near him; and this is [the meaning of] "he tears his own soul in his anger," for he tears his soul and settles a strange god in its place — for what is he reckoned? And he is called idolatry, and whoever speaks with him is as though he joined himself to actual idolatry, for actual idolatry dwells within him, and it is forbidden to gaze upon his face, and of him it is written, "do not turn to idols," and concerning this it is written, "you shall not make for yourself molten gods." And all impurities have a purification except this one, because it defiles the body from within and without, and defiles the whole soul; and even if this person comes and uproots the sitra achra from within himself entirely and forever, and afterward strives to sanctify himself and to draw that holy soul upon himself, then would that he be sanctified — for since it was once uprooted from him, how much must the person do until it returns to its place]:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:20: Touchiness is a branch of pride and of anger. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Rosh Hashanah 17a), whoever is touchy is dealt with in kind, and his sins are not forgiven him, as it is said (Micah 7:18), "who bears iniquity and passes over transgression" — to whom does He bear iniquity? To one who passes over transgression [committed against him] — but one who forgives those who wrong him, and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:21: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 32a), a person should always seek mercy every day and every hour, should put his mouth to the dust, should offer his cheek to the one who strikes him, and be filled with disgrace; happy is he who hears his own disgrace and does not respond, and so Isaiah says (Isaiah 3:6), "a people I have given to those who strike them."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:22: So the Sages said (Rosh Hashanah 17a), whoever forgives those who wrong him — his own transgressions are all forgiven him, as it is said, "who bears iniquity and passes over transgression," and so on,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:23: and they said, in the name of Elijah of blessed memory (end of Reishit Chochmah, Gate 3): there are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, loves — one who does not become angry, one who does not become drunk, and one who does not insist on his own way; and Rabbi Akiva asked (Megillah 28a) Rabbi Nechunya the Great, by what merit have you lived so long? And he answered him, in all my days I never accepted gifts, and I never insisted on my own way.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:24: And they said (Rosh Hashanah 17a): Rav Huna bar Yehoshua fell ill; they said to him, what do you see [in a vision]? He said to them, thus said the Holy One, blessed be He: since he does not insist on his own way, do not insist on your own way with him, as it is said, "who bears iniquity and passes over transgression"; and they said, Rav Nachman dug up a mound and found Rav Achai bar Yoshiah buried there, and saw him whole in his bones; they said to him, what is this? He told them, in all my days I never insisted on my own way, nor did I hold in my heart envy of my fellow, as it is said (Proverbs 14:30), "and envy is the rot of the bones."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:25: And they said (Ta'anit 25b): it once happened that Rabbi Eliezer went down before the ark [to lead the prayers for rain] and was not answered, and so on; Rabbi Akiva went down and was answered, and a heavenly voice came forth and said, "it is because this one forgives those who wrong him."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:26: And they said (Chullin 89a), the world endures only for the sake of one who restrains his mouth at the time of a quarrel, as it is said (Job 26:7), "He hangs the earth upon nothing (belimah)"; Rabbi Abahu says, this refers to one who makes himself as though he were nothing, and so on; and our Rabbis taught (Shabbat 88b): those who are insulted but do not insult, who hear their own disgrace but do not respond, of them Scripture says (Judges 5:31), "and they who love Him are like the sun going forth in its might,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:27: and Elijah, of blessed memory, said (Eliyahu Zuta ch. 4), always be one who is treated with contempt by other people, and by your own household more than all others; and Elijah our father, of blessed memory, said (Kallah Rabbati end of ch. 5), the Torah is expounded only to one who is not touchy, and I too reveal Myself only to one who is not touchy:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:28: Sadness causes the prevention of divine service and the fulfillment of the commandments, and nullifies engagement in Torah study and the intention of prayer, and nullifies good thoughts about serving the Lord, and it is the gate through which the incitement of the evil inclination begins, even for a tzaddik, by showing him that he has no benefit from his service, since he suffers afflictions, and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:29: And also, it comes upon him under the guise of piety, saying to him: how can it enter your mind, dust, maggot, and worm that you are, to draw near and be sanctified with the holiness of the King of the world? As it is written (Proverbs 25:7), "deep things are too wondrous for a fool," and as it is written (Job 35:7), "if you are righteous, what do you give Him?"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:30: It also causes the removal of the Holy Spirit from a person, whereas the opposite occurs when he serves the blessed Lord with joy, as it is written (Psalms 100:2), "serve the Lord with gladness," for joy adds great desire and love to cleave to Him, blessed be He; and it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and with gladness of heart," and so on — for if the service is done with sadness, it is like a servant who serves his master with a sad and sullen face.
